correctness.rationale: The normalized killed backward PDE is uniformly elliptic on the fixed annulus. Analytic weak-speed perturbation gives the exact first- and second-order angular Fourier equations. The homogeneous-Bessel substitution gives an exact boundary integral identity. Matched large-argument I1,K1 expansions yield C_beta=-S beta^-3/2/(2L)+O(beta^-2) and B_beta second derivative h(1)beta^-1/2/2+O(beta^-1). Taylor expansion on the beta^-1 outer strip gives the quadratic, whose positive simple root is explicit. sinh(t)>t proves S>0 for every 0<alpha<1 and h(1)<0. The Bessel-vs-BVP standalone diagnostics passed 171 assertions. The high-beta result applies to the weak-speed coefficient only; no finite-speed joint limit was inferred.

value.rationale: The exact outer-wall beta^-1 positive skin in a two-absorber annulus is physically and mathematically motivated: the fast-angular-mixing effective-diffusion approximation predicts faster exit at fixed interior positions but misses a strict opposite weak-activity sign arbitrarily near the outer absorber. The explicit layer polynomial and sharp zero location supply a nontrivial boundary nonuniformity benchmark across every annulus aspect ratio, not an arbitrary isolated parameter slice. Small amplitude and restricted sequential limits are stated.
